claim: For every fixed integer \(k\ge 1\), deciding whether a sentence \(\varphi\) of monadic first-order logic with equality and the infinity quantifiers is monotone in a designated unary predicate \(P\), over possibly empty domains and with exactly \(k\) unary predicates in the input signature, is \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-hardness already holds for \(k=1\) in the first-order sublanguage without infinity quantifiers.

correctness.rationale: The non-monotonicity sentence exactly encodes a same-domain inclusion and a true-to-false change. Fixed-vocabulary rank-\(q\) type truncation gives polynomially many classes; the symbolic evaluation procedure stores only a bounded assignment pattern and truncated type counts. The two-element QBF construction proves \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-hardness and is polynomial in input size.
